beats.headline: Intel Jumps 11.4% on Musk Terafab and Apollo Deal
beats.explanation: Intel surged 11.42% to close at $58.95 on 1.8x average volume following news that it is joining Elon Musk's Terafab AI chip project. Investor sentiment was also supported by Intel repurchasing Apollo's 49% stake in the Fab 34 Ireland joint venture for $14.2 billion to regain full ownership. The rally was largely company-specific, outpacing peers like competitor AMD (+4.64%) and supplier ASML (+8.77%).

beats.headline: Intel Soars 23.6% on Q1 Beat and Strong Guidance
beats.explanation: Intel climbed 23.60% to $82.54 with volume 2.8x its 30-day average after delivering a Q1 earnings beat, reporting revenue up 7.2% year-over-year to $13.58 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $0.29. Next-quarter revenue guidance midpoint of $14.3 billion surpassed analyst projections by 9.2%. Competitor AMD also rose 13.91% after an analyst upgrade tied to Intel's report, while competitor AAPL dipped 0.87%.

beats.headline: Intel Rallies 12.1% on Google Packaging Report
beats.explanation: Intel gained 12.10% to reach $94.75 on 2.3x normal volume, driven by renewed optimism around its foundry turnaround under CEO Lip-Bu Tan. A report stated that Alphabet plans to adopt Intel's EMIB packaging technology for next-generation TPU chips, alongside reports of severe industrywide CPU shortages. Intel outperformed its broader peer group, including competitor NVDA which declined 1.84% and competitor AMD which gained 4.30%.

beats.headline: Intel Surges 12.9% on Potential Apple Supply Talks
beats.explanation: Intel gained 12.91% to $108.15 on 1.9x average volume after reports revealed preliminary discussions with Apple regarding manufacturing chips at Intel's U.S. facilities. The prospective deal positions Intel Foundry as an alternative domestic supplier to TSMC, prompting TSMC shares to slide 1.79% while competitor QCOM rallied 10.79%.

beats.headline: Intel Advances 14.0% on Preliminary Apple Deal
beats.explanation: Intel surged 13.96% to $124.92 on 2.2x normal volume after reports confirmed a preliminary chipmaking agreement between Apple and Intel, backed by White House support. The move was company-specific upside compared to competitor and supplier TSM, which fell 0.60%, though competitor AMD gained 11.44% amid broader CPU enthusiasm.

beats.headline: Intel Pulls Back 5.1% in Company-Specific Dip
beats.explanation: Intel dropped 5.14% to $114.68 on 1.9x average volume without negative company-specific news, despite announcing a $3.3 billion substrate plant investment in India. The retreat came as peers displayed mixed trading, with competitors AVGO (+4.73%) and MSFT (+5.45%) gaining while GOOGL declined 2.51% and TSM fell 1.51%.

beats.headline: Intel Rallies 11.2% on Google 3M TPU Foundry Order
beats.explanation: Intel climbed 11.19% to $110.27 on reports that Alphabet committed to ordering over 3 million custom AI TPUs from Intel Foundry for 2028 production. In addition, Cadence expanded its collaboration with Intel Foundry for 14A process optimization. Intel led semiconductor peers, outpacing competitor AMD (+5.13%) and supplier ASML (+6.54%).

beats.headline: Intel Advances 9.3% After Bank of America Upgrade
beats.explanation: Intel shares rose 9.27% to close at $116.96 after Bank of America issued a rare double upgrade from Underperform to Buy, lifting its price objective from $96 to $135. The upgrade cited improving CPU demand and growing confidence in the contract manufacturing business, with semiconductor peer ASML gaining 9.53% and competitor AMD up 7.97%.

beats.headline: Intel Rises 10.6% on Executive Hire and Apple Buzz
beats.explanation: Intel surged 10.64% to $133.99 with volume 2.3x normal after appointing former SK Hynix CEO Seok-Hee Lee to lead its foundry advanced packaging business. Momentum was further amplified by public comments from President Trump touting Intel's domestic chipmaking pact with Apple. Peers also advanced, with supplier and competitor TSM rising 6.93% and competitor QCOM gaining 6.17%.

beats.headline: Intel Drops 9.7% Amid Broader Chip Selloff
beats.explanation: Intel tumbled 9.66% to $110.39 despite receiving a Street-high $200 price target from HSBC. The selloff was shared across the semiconductor space, sparked by Samsung Electronics earnings triggering concerns over AI chip valuations; competitor AMD sank 6.51% and supplier ASML declined 4.26%.

beats.headline: Intel Drops 7.9% Post-Earnings on Capex Concerns
beats.explanation: Intel dropped 7.89% to $92.32 following its Q2 financial results, reversing initial premarket strength as investors focused on escalating capital expenditure plans required for its foundry buildout. While revenue grew 25% and beat forecasts by $1.7 billion, spending worries weighed heavily. The retreat outpaced peers, as competitor AMD dipped 3.29% and supplier TSM dropped 2.93%.

beats.headline: Intel Gains 12.1% on AI Agent CPU Demand Wave
beats.explanation: Intel jumped 12.14% to $121.78 on 1.9x average volume, lifted by optimism surrounding CPU compute demand fueled by Meta's Muse AI agent. The surge was part of an industrywide rally in processing silicon, with competitor AMD jumping 9.95% and competitor QCOM advancing 9.29%.

The stock's dramatic climb from $52.91 in early April to above $133 in mid-June was powered by commercial validation of Intel Foundry, highlighted by Elon Musk's Terafab initiative, preliminary manufacturing agreements with Apple, and a 3-million-unit TPU order from Alphabet. Although strong operational progress was affirmed by blowout Q1 and Q2 revenue beats, the summer brought volatility as sector-wide earnings jitters and investor anxiety over elevated foundry capital expenditures triggered sharp pullbacks in July. By late September, renewed enthusiasm around CPU utilization for agentic AI applications helped the stock recover back to $121.78, establishing Intel Foundry as a viable domestic alternative to TSMC while underscoring that heavy infrastructure investment remains a persistent source of sentiment swings.
